differences.title: 1. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Dragonfly employs a multi-threaded, shared-nothing architecture, enabling it to fully utilize modern multi-core CPUs for enhanced parallelism and throughput.
differences.rightDesc: Redis traditionally uses a single-threaded event loop for command execution, simplifying its core but potentially creating a bottleneck on multi-core systems.

differences.title: 2. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Thanks to its multi-threaded design and optimized memory management (using its own memory allocator), Dragonfly achieves significantly higher operations per second.
differences.rightDesc: Redis offers excellent performance, especially for single-threaded workloads, but can be limited by its event loop on very high-concurrency scenarios.

differences.title: 3. MEMORY MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Dragonfly uses its own sophisticated memory allocator, designed for efficiency and reduced fragmentation, leading to better memory utilization and performance.
differences.rightDesc: Redis typically relies on system allocators (like jemalloc or glibc malloc), which are general-purpose and may not be as optimized for Redis's access patterns.

differences.title: 4. COMPATIBILITY
differences.leftDesc: Dragonfly is designed for drop-in compatibility with Redis and Memcached APIs, allowing easy migration and integration with existing applications.
differences.rightDesc: Redis implements its own robust protocol and command set, which is the standard that many clients and tools interact with.

differences.title: 5. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Dragonfly integrates sharding capabilities natively within its architecture, simplifying distributed deployments and management for horizontal scaling.
differences.rightDesc: Redis often requires external solutions like Redis Cluster, Twemproxy, or client-side logic for effective sharding and horizontal scaling.

differences.title: 6. RESILIENCE
differences.leftDesc: Both support robust persistence mechanisms like RDB snapshots and Append-Only File (AOF) logging to ensure data durability upon restarts.
differences.rightDesc: Both support robust persistence mechanisms like RDB snapshots and Append-Only File (AOF) logging to ensure data durability upon restarts.

differences.title: 7. DEVELOPMENT
differences.leftDesc: Dragonfly is written in modern C++, leveraging advanced language features for performance and maintainability in its complex, multi-threaded design.
differences.rightDesc: Redis is written predominantly in C, a language known for its performance and low-level control, which has served it well for decades.
